title: Notable physics papers — arXiv announcement batch, Tue 6 Oct 2026
global_caveat: ArXiv publishes no official trending chart. The order is inferred from checkable results, cross-field relevance, journal or independent coverage where available, and methodological contribution; it is not a popularity ranking. This is a very fresh batch with limited citation signal.

sections.title: Detection of knots in the supernova type Iax remnant Pa 30
sections.abstract: Deep Gemini North images resolve Pa 30's ejecta filaments into cascades of knots, reveal matching [O III] emission, and constrain any transverse kick of the central star.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find about ten times more [S II] filaments than previous studies, resolve them as knot chains rather than smooth radial streaks, and set a 3σ transverse-kick upper limit of roughly 100 km/s.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; narrowband Gemini North/GMOS imaging in [S II] and [O III].
sections.unique_caveat: Individual knots are close to the image-resolution limit: median [S II] filament width is 0.7 arcsec against 0.50-arcsec seeing; Pa 30 is one remnant, not a population study.

sections.title: Forming Molecular Hydrogen in a Galaxy Halo Through Star Formation Wind Interactions
sections.abstract: Absorption measurements identify cold H₂ 139 kpc from a starburst galaxy—the most distant direct H₂ detection from a galaxy reported by the authors—and point to wind–halo interactions as a possible formation route.
sections.claimed_result: From absorption toward a background sightline, the authors infer H₂ at about 139 kpc, moving at about 100 km/s relative to its host and with a cold excitation temperature near 245 K; they argue a star-formation-driven wind interacting with halo gas may have formed it.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; absorption spectroscopy with HST/COS and supporting MMT/VLT data, interpreted with ionization/formation modeling.
sections.unique_caveat: The wind-driven formation history is inferred rather than directly observed, and the claim rests on one cloud/sightline; the authors flag substantial uncertainty in the H I measurement.

sections.title: Energy-constrained two-way capacities of the pure-loss bosonic channel
sections.abstract: For an ideal pure-loss optical channel with mean transmitted photon number N, the paper proves that four two-way communication capacities coincide at g(N) − g((1−η)N).
sections.claimed_result: Under an unconditional mean-photon-number constraint, the two-way quantum, entanglement-distribution, private, and secret-key capacities are all equal to the stated formula; the paper also derives strong-converse thresholds for specified models.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; information-theoretic converse proofs and capacity-achieving protocol analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is for the ideal pure-loss channel and specified energy constraints; it is not an experimental demonstration or a capacity formula for general thermal/noisy optical channels.

sections.title: How to scale your HEP ML models: A recipe for robust architecture comparisons at scale
sections.abstract: The authors develop a procedure for measuring compute/data scaling and compare multi-task transformer choices using the roughly 11-billion-jet ATLAS JetSet2 dataset.
sections.claimed_result: The paper proposes and validates a workflow for robust scaling-law fits, first on toy problems and then on HEP transformer tasks, comparing multiple fitting approaches and architecture/task choices.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; training and scaling studies on toy data and ATLAS JetSet2.
sections.unique_caveat: Scaling behavior is empirical and depends on selected tasks, inputs, training budget, and dataset; it is not a universal law for all HEP models or experiments.

sections.title: Polynomial-time classical algorithms for mean-field models up to the glass transition
sections.abstract: A rigorous quantum-cavity approach yields polynomial-time estimates of local thermal observables for the SYK model and extends to classical mean-field spin glasses up to their transition.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give polynomial-time classical algorithms for local thermal expectations in SYK at constant temperatures and for classical spin glasses up to the phase transition; they also describe a quantum algorithm for learning SYK Hamiltonians from Gibbs-state data.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; rigorous cavity-method analysis with complexity bounds.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantees concern local thermal expectations and specific mean-field model classes at constant temperatures; they do not imply efficient reconstruction of a full many-body state or tractability of generic finite-dimensional systems.

sections.title: Exact vortex decomposition of the shift current
sections.abstract: The authors decompose shift conductivity into an integer-winding contribution and continuous terms, deriving the response from singularities of the shift vector on the Brillouin torus.
sections.claimed_result: In graphene–Haldane and biased AB bilayer models, the integer sector alone accounts for the band-edge peak when a charge lies at the band edge and trigonal warping is present; the relevant integer is the winding of that charge.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; analytic decomposition and model calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is established for the stated models and conditions; the abstract does not report experimental verification or a general claim that the Chern number fixes shift-current sign.

sections.title: Novel dependence between neutrino mass splittings strongly supported by initial JUNO results
sections.abstract: The author compares an empirically proposed relation between neutrino mass splittings with JUNO's early precision measurements and finds close numerical agreement.
sections.claimed_result: For the measured mass-squared splittings, the paper obtains 1.4143 with reported uncertainty of about 0.0037, close to √2, and argues this is consistent with an additional parameter relation.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data interpretation; comparison with JUNO's reported oscillation measurements, not a new JUNO measurement.
sections.unique_caveat: The relation is empirically motivated, and numerical agreement with one set of measurements does not establish a new symmetry or independent physical constraint.
